question: Does the portable orderer scorer+allocator (O2: OrdererScoreModel -> allocate_suborders) match or beat the proportional baseline on held-out scale topologies, distilled from the proportional throughput teacher?

method.deploy: scorer_ordering_policy -> per-producer scores tiled across k_stream slots -> decode_ordering -> allocate_suborders (masked, conserved)
method.teacher: per-producer log(makeable_qty_now) (proportional throughput signal), masked MSE distillation
method.held_out: seeds 6-9, depth 3 (varied economics; producer count constant at this depth)

metric: consumer_completed_units ratio vs proportional baseline (per held-out seed); mean + min ratio
pass: scorer+allocator loads/runs on all held-out topologies (versatility, already proven by contract gates) AND mean ratio vs proportional >= 1.0 with no death (value).
notes: Versatility (variable P, relabel, row-permutation) proven locally in tests/test_orderer_scorer.py. This run measures VALUE vs the deterministic baseline. Producer-count transfer (different P) is a follow-up: depth fixed here keeps P constant across held-out seeds.
